prompt.context: Your client is a gift wrapping paper manufacturer in the United States. They are considering a proposal to outsource their manufacturing to mainland China. You have been called in to assist in the go / no-go decision making process.
prompt.question: Should the client outsource their manufacturing to mainland China? Please provide your thoughts and a recommendation.

clarifying_info.q: What are the fixed costs in the US?
clarifying_info.a: Plant & machinery: 5 units at $20 each = $100 per ream. Employees: 25 workers at $2 each = $50 ... wait, see exhibit — US: 1 unit Parts & Machines at $100 each, 1 Employee at $100 each per ream.
Raw paper material: $20 per ream (same in both locations). Ink: $100 per ream in the US, $50 per ream in China.

clarifying_info.q: What are the production requirements in China?
clarifying_info.a: China: 5 units Parts & Machines at $20 each = $100, 1 Employee at $50 each = $50 per ream.

clarifying_info.q: What is the shipping cost from China to the US?
clarifying_info.a: Shipping from China to US is $150 per ream.

exhibits.title: Gift Wrapping Paper Production Comparability Between Markets
exhibits.shows: Side-by-side comparison of production inputs and unit costs for manufacturing one ream of gift wrapping paper in the United States versus China, showing parts & machines quantities and costs, and employee quantities and costs.
exhibits.data: US: 1 Unit Parts & Machines at $100 each, 1 Employee at $100 each, 1 Ream Paper. China: 5 Units Parts & Machines at $20 each, 1 Employee at $50 each, 1 Ream Paper.

framework: Establish all-in cost per ream for US manufacturing (fixed + variable)
Establish all-in cost per ream for China manufacturing including shipping
Compare total loaded costs for both options
Identify the cost drivers and key swing factors
Generate a recommendation with risks and next steps

questions.prompt: What is the total cost per ream of manufacturing in the United States?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify and sum all cost components: Parts & Machines, Labor, Paper, and Ink. Strong answer clearly categorizes fixed vs variable costs and arrives at $320 total.

math.setup: Sum all US cost components per ream

questions.prompt: What is the total cost per ream of manufacturing in China, fully loaded with shipping?
questions.guidance: Candidate should use China-specific labor and equipment costs, note lower ink cost, but crucially add the $150 shipping cost. Strong answer arrives at $370 total and flags that shipping is the key deal-breaker.

math.setup: Sum all China cost components per ream plus shipping to US

questions.prompt: Compare the two options and identify the key cost driver making China less attractive.
questions.guidance: Shipping cost of $150 per ream is the deal-breaker. Without shipping, China would cost $220 vs US $320 — a $100 saving. But shipping adds $150, making China $50 more expensive. Candidate should also note that China saves on ink ($50 vs $100) and labor ($50 vs $100) but these are offset by the high shipping cost.

math.setup: Compare US total vs China total, and assess the impact of shipping alone
steps: China total without shipping: $220 (saves $100 vs US)
China total with shipping: $370 (costs $50 more than US)
Shipping alone swings the decision by $150
math.answer: China is $50 more expensive per ream once shipping is included; shipping is the single deal-breaker

brainstorming.prompt: What alternatives or additional considerations might make China more attractive in the future, or what other issues should the client track?

categories.name: Reducing shipping costs
ideas: Bulk shipping to lower per-unit freight cost
Shipping flat sheets instead of rolls to improve container density
Nearshoring to Mexico as an intermediate option

categories.name: Cost trends to monitor in China
ideas: Ink prices in China (currently $50 vs $100 in US — track if prices converge)
Paper costs (currently same — monitor for divergence)
Chinese labor cost inflation reducing the labor advantage
Parts & machine repair/maintenance costs may increase with 5 units vs 1

categories.name: Operational complexity
ideas: More machines to manage in China increases repair and downtime risk
Hiring and firing costs in China may increase total labor cost beyond wage rate
Supply chain and quality control complexity across geographies
Currency risk (RMB appreciation eroding cost advantage)

categories.name: US shutdown costs
ideas: Severance and employee transition costs not examined
Stranded asset value of existing US machinery

recommendation: Do not outsource to China at this time — fully loaded cost of $370/ream in China exceeds $320/ream in the US by $50 per ream
Shipping cost of $150/ream is the primary deal-breaker; it more than offsets labor and ink savings achieved in China
risks: Chinese labor costs are rising and the current $50/employee advantage may erode
If shipping costs decline (e.g., bulk or flat-sheet shipping), the economics could flip in China's favor
US shutdown costs have not been examined and could be significant
next_steps: Track ink costs, paper costs, and employee wage trends in China to monitor long-term viability of a move
Explore whether shipping costs can be reduced through bulk shipping or alternative packaging formats
Quantify US plant shutdown costs before ruling out future outsourcing scenarios
